message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking.  In practice the tower’s owners schedule a full repaint every seven years, and each cycle normally takes **about six months** (roughly 180 days).  

That figure comes from:

| Factor | Typical value |
|--------|---------------|
| Surface area to be covered | ~10 000 m² (including all panels, rails, and rivets) |
| Crew size | 10–20 skilled painters working on scaffolds and platforms |
| Work rate | 50–100 m² per worker per day (depending on height, weather, and safety constraints) |
| Coats required | 3–4 layers (primer + 2–3 paint coats) |
| Downtime | Weather delays, inspections, and safety checks add ~10–15 % extra time |

So, if you had a dedicated crew and favorable weather, you could finish in about **6 months**.  If conditions were less ideal—rain, wind, or logistical hiccups—the job could stretch to 8–9 months.
